findingDetails.title: Session-expiry exception can be read as client-side authorization
findingDetails.claim: M33 permits a client-side redirect when a session expires while the page is open and never says data calls must still be refused server-side, so a reader can treat the UX redirect as the authorization boundary.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the three new references for any other authentication or authorization statement; M33 is the only one, and its own Why states the flash-of-data risk it then re-permits.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A reader may assume server authorization is unchanged; the item does not say so, and the 'server is no longer in the loop' wording actively suggests otherwise.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if web-performance-and-loading.md or the surface's workflow docs already state the server-side refusal requirement for the same case.
findingDetails.scopeProof: grep for auth in the three new references returns only M33; no adjacent item covers session expiry.
